method.filters: RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook (lp, hp, bp constant 0 dB peak, peaking EQ); formants are two-pole resonators in the Klatt 1980 cascade form with unit DC gain; notches are cookbook peaking cuts (unity away from the notch)
method.encoding: each section mapped to the engine's five values and encoded with its 16-bit word encoder; unused sections are the identity row; low-gain numerators are carried by a gain word that is an exact power-of-two multiple of a pole word so word interpolation keeps the level
method.phasers_and_flanger: X3 grammar, re-authored with rounded numbers read from the decoded EmulatorX menu tables (report/0923/x3-raw-tables): Phaser A = PhazeShift1/Phaser 1 (two notches two octaves apart, zeros 2 Hz wide on the circle, pole partner at the notch and 1 kHz wide at Q0, at 0.72 x the notch and 62 Hz wide at Q100 with -5.5 dB; lower stage's M0 Q0 pole real), Phaser B = PhazeShift2/Phaser 2 (same grammar, notch spacing changing with Morph), Flanger 3 = FlangerLite (octave notch pair, a resonance near the upper notch, a pole-only resonance below, Q sharpens the poles and adds up to +4.5 dB); the Smith allpass phaser and comb-notch flanger below were the previous candidate and are kept as functions
method.phasers: Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Phasing with First-Order Allpass Filters' (https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Phasing_First_Order_Allpass_Filters.html): H = (1 + g prod AP1(a_i)) / (1 + g), AP1 = (a + z^-1)/(1 + a z^-1), six stages, factored by roots into three biquads, each section unit DC gain; Morph = stage break frequency (a_i by tan(pi fb/fs)), Q = depth g; Phaser A six equal stages (Mo'Phatt PhazeShift1), Phaser B three stages at fb/1.5 and three at fb*1.5 (our choice for PhazeShift2 'slightly different notch frequency')
method.flanger: custom three-notch approximation of Smith's comb y = x + g x(n-M) (PASP 'Flanging', https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Flanging.html): second-order notch sections at 1, 3, 5 x f0 (the comb's first three notches), pole radius exp(-pi f0/fs) so each -3 dB width is f0 Hz as in the comb, zero radius set for notch depth (1-g)/(1+g), unit DC per section; Mo'Phatt FlangerLite 'three notches, frequency moves frequency and spacing'
method.vowels: Peterson and Barney 1952, adult male averages for /a/, /i/, /u/ (F1-F3); formant bandwidths 90/110/170 Hz are our choice
method.check: 65 x 17 Morph x Q states, floor word interpolation as the engine does, response 20 Hz-20 kHz
